messages: maya: Pushed a new compact-layout mock for the Usage dashboard. Main asks: make spend rows scannable, surface invoice CTA, decide where scope switching lives. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/compact-usage-v4 sam: Quick take: global header toggle is simplest. But power users want per-row scope so they can compare project vs org. Could we surface a tiny scope swatch on hover instead of always-on pills? jo: Hover-only swatch worries accessibility. Hover states disappear on keyboard/mobile. I prefer a micro pill (10-12px tall) always visible, low contrast. If global toggle is default, advanced compare flips to per-row pills. devon: Engineering note: per-row scopes = more aggregation calls. We can batch on the client into one payload, but backend still needs to support multi-scope aggregations. Spike needed. Also recommend pooling canvas sparklines rather than many SVGs. maya: For launch, let's do global toggle + an "Advanced compare" switch to unblock. Jo please mock both flows so folks can see tradeoffs. neil: Perf watch: ghost invoice CTAs and hover expansions must not create new DOM nodes per row; reuse elements. Also add a telemetry flag so we can measure extra requests when per-row is enabled. sam: UX nit: invoice link is too subtle. Make it a secondary ghost button that shows month + amount (e.g., "Invoice Jun $2.1K") and becomes primary on hover. That helps finance users scan quickly. jo: Accessibility: token numbers in compact rows fail contrast. Suggest label "Est. tokens (total)" and use medium weight for numbers. Add aria-label with full integer. Example: 12.3k. design-bot: Reminder: design sync Friday 10:30am. Agenda: compact rollout, invoice affordance, accessibility fixes. maya: Action items: Jo update artboards (global + per-row + contrast variant), Devon spike batching & canvas sparklines, Neil add telemetry note, Sam validate CTA copy widths. Back in on Friday. :thumbsup:
